rows.grounds: compound denoting an army with four divisions; object of conquering
absolutive expressing prior action of victory
genitive plural indicating the beings affected
compound agent noun describing one who brings about immobilization

items.question: What power over armies and camels is attributed to Vaṭuka?
premises: Vaṭuka is described as having conquered a four-limbed army.
Vaṭuka is described as causing paralysis of camels.
These actions present Vaṭuka as a subduing and immobilizing force.
items.inference: Vaṭuka possesses the power to defeat organized military forces and to paralyze camels.
uncertainties: The exact referent of the four-limbed army in this ritual context is not specified.
items.plain_english: Having conquered a four-limbed army, he causes the paralysis of camels.
